transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, the main reason I’m here is that I'm really struggling at work. I'm a nurse, and when I'm on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. 

It's like... if an IV pump beeps, or I hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off down the hall, my mind just gets pulled away. And then suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was even in the middle of working on. It's happening a lot, and I really need to figure out what's going on.
Does this trouble with losing your train of thought happen to you in other parts of your life, outside of work?

I'm... not really sure, actually. I haven't really noticed it happening as much outside of the hospital. Or at least, I guess work is just where it really stands out to me because the stakes are higher and there's so much going on. I haven't really paid attention to whether it happens when I'm just at home.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?
No, not really. I mean, nursing can be stressful, obviously, but I don't feel anxious or on edge in general. It's really just the trouble keeping my focus that's the problem.
Can you think of any situations outside of work where you had difficulty focusing or were easily distracted?

I really can't think of anything specific right now. Like I said, I just haven't really paid attention to it outside of the hospital. When I'm at home, I guess there aren't as many things competing for my attention, or maybe it just doesn't matter as much if I lose my train of thought. But yeah, nothing really comes to mind.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse or doing things without thinking them through?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really do things on impulse. I'm usually pretty careful about what I do, especially being a nurse. It's really just the focus and losing my train of thought that's been the issue, not so much acting without thinking.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still enjoy my usual hobbies when I have the time for them. It's not that I don't want to do things... my interest in them is definitely still there. Like I said, it's really just the focusing part that's giving me trouble.
Do you ever find that your thoughts feel disorganized or hard to put into words?

No, I don't think my thoughts are disorganized, and I don't usually have trouble putting them into words. I mean, if I lose my train of thought, I might stop talking for a second because I forgot what I was saying, but the thoughts themselves make sense to me. I can explain things fine, as long as I can hold onto the thought long enough to get it out.
Have you noticed any changes in your level of energy or activity recently?

Not really, no. My energy is about the same as it usually is. I mean, working as a nurse, I definitely get tired after a long shift, but that's just normal tiredness. I haven't noticed any weird drops in my energy, and I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything either. My activity level has been pretty steady.
When did you first notice that you were having trouble keeping your focus at work?

Well, it's been a major problem for almost two years now. That was right around the time I took on expanded charge-nurse responsibilities at work. Since I started those new duties, keeping my focus has just been really difficult.
Do you think you would have this trouble keeping your focus if you were working in a quieter, less busy environment?

I'm not really sure, honestly. Working in a hospital, it's never exactly quiet, so I haven't really had the chance to find out. I guess it might be a little easier without all the monitors alarming and people constantly talking, but... I don't know. I feel like I'd probably still have a hard time with it, but it's hard to say for sure since I haven't been in that kind of environment.
Have you ever had trouble focusing or paying attention in school?

Yes, I did. Even way back in elementary school... my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was always losing my worksheets, or I'd just forget to turn in my homework entirely. My mom actually had to sit down with me every single night while I did my assignments, just to keep me on track.
Do you feel overwhelmed or stressed when you lose your train of thought at work?

Yes, very much so. It's incredibly stressful. Um, the concerns at work have actually gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision right now. Because I lose my track of what I'm doing, other nurses have to double-check parts of my charge-nurse follow-through just to make sure things get done. It's... well, it makes me feel like I’m becoming a liability to the team instead of a leader.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a child, before you started school?

I honestly don't remember much from before I started school. My mom has never mentioned anything about me being particularly hyper or having trouble sitting still back then, so I don't think so. It really just seemed to become an issue once I had schoolwork and things I actually needed to focus on.
Did you have any behavioral problems or difficulties in school besides trouble with focusing and paying attention when you were a child?

No, not really. Um, I didn't have any behavioral problems. I wasn't getting sent to the principal's office or acting out in class or anything like that. It was pretty much just the... the losing my work and forgetting assignments that I mentioned. But behavior-wise, no, I was fine.
Are you more easily distracted or have trouble focusing when you're doing things you enjoy, like your hobbies?

No, not really. Um, if it's something I actually enjoy doing, I don't usually have any trouble focusing on it. I can usually stick with my hobbies just fine. It's really just the work tasks or... or the things I have to do where I get so distracted.
Have you experienced difficulties with focus or paying attention consistently throughout your life?

Yes, it really has been pretty consistent. Um, even way back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always losing my worksheets or just forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track and make sure I actually finished things. So, yeah, it's been an issue for as long as I've been in school.
Do you think your focus issues would improve if you were to switch to a less demanding or less busy role at work?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... being a nurse, it's pretty much always busy, so I haven't really had a less demanding role to compare it to. But... I don't think it would actually fix the problem. Even on the rare days when the floor is quiet and I have a lot less going on, I still catch myself losing track of what I'm supposed to be doing or forgetting things. So... no, I don't really think it's just about how busy I am.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with focus or paying attention during most years of your life since childhood?

Yeah, um, like I mentioned just a minute ago, it really has been a lifelong thing for me. From childhood all the way through now, I've always struggled with it. So, yes, definitely most years of my life.
